slides.role: body: building is the easy part
slides.heading: shipping is the easy part
body:
shipping an app used to be
the hard part.

today ai gets you there in a weekend.
same for every other founder.

so your app isn't the edge anymore.
getting it seen is.

cutout.note: heavyset office worker leaning on a beige CRT monitor, cheesy double thumbs up

slides.heading: distribution is the game
body:
the apps growing right now
aren't the best built ones.
they're the ones you keep seeing.

i break down tiktoks that blow up.
one was a single selfie with one
question on it. 17.4 million views.
no face cam. no editing. no ad budget.
simple slideshows are still winning.

cutout.note: man in a dark suit leaning in, tapping his temple, sly smirk

slides.heading: let ai make the content
body:
founders rarely stop posting
because it doesn't work.
they stop because it takes forever.

so stop making posts from scratch.
take formats that already pull views
and remake them for your product.

i did this with Amplify and got
30 posts for my saas. for free.
(Amplify is the link in my bio)

cutout.note: man in a Hawaiian shirt and sunglasses on a beach lounger, laptop on his belly, drink in hand

slides.heading: post twice a day
body:
one post a week is a lottery ticket.
two a day is a system.

make a week of posts in one sitting,
schedule two a day on TikTok,
and stop posting by hand.

more posts means more data.
more data means you find
what works faster.

cutout.note: woman in a boxy blazer holding up a flip phone in each hand, triumphant shout

slides.heading: kill what flops
body:
give it two weeks and you'll see it.
a few formats pull views. most don't.

stop posting the ones that stall.
make ten more of the ones that hit.

your next winner is usually
a remix of your last one.

cutout.note: man in a shirt and loose tie tossing a crumpled paper over his shoulder

slides.heading: the short version
body: build less. post more.

no team, no ad budget.
just a system you repeat every week.
Amplify is the link in my bio.

cutout.note: woman in a 90s power suit spread back in an executive chair, satisfied boss smile
